title: Letter 33 — Mercy, and Not Sacrifice
attribution_note: Letter 33 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: A warm church, not a high one

pairs.en: I thank you for your love. What I said to you concerning the church, I now explain in writing, and give this counsel: make the church not high, so that it may serve both for summer and for winter — that is, a warm church, with a stove. Take your example from the newly built cathedral church at Voronezh, and I do not advise you to raise it high. You will have less expense. The peasants will not be heavily burdened; and for those who come, and for the priest with the clergy, and for yourselves, it is quieter and more willing to stand in a warm church; and you yourselves may acknowledge this for the truth.

And as for the boasters who wish to raise themselves up to the clouds, yet inhumanly flay the last skin from the peasants — do not listen to them, and do not imitate them. One day they will see that in so building churches they serve not the glory of God, but their own whims and vainglory; and churches raised high will help them nothing, when they see the peasants' tears poured out before the dread Judge Christ, and they will be terrified and come into confusion. For what profit is it to build temples, and to destroy living temples? To raise high walls, and leave the peasants half-naked, without food, salt and what is needful for life? This is tyranny, and not the worship of God!
Christ says in the Gospel: *“I will have mercy, and not sacrifice”* [Matthew 9:13; 12:7]. Consider what I write. Take long counsel, and think, and then build.
I counsel and write to you, in very truth, for your good. May God give you understanding and help. Commending you with all your household to Him, I remain your servant and well-wisher,
